2607.24236.title: CAGE: Cognitive Attribution Graphs for Faithful Inline Citation Generation in Long-Form Question Answering
2607.24236.paper_summary: Long-form question answering increasingly relies on retrieved evidence to make LLM outputs verifiable, with inline citations tracing claims to source documents. However, existing systems often attach citations that are topically related but insufficient to support their claims. We identify attribution ambiguity as a structural challenge: end-to-end generation must implicitly resolve combinatorial claim--document assignments, obscuring evidential boundaries and increasing the risk of evidence-boundary overrun, where claims exceed cited support. To address this challenge, we propose CAGE (Cognitive Attribution Graphs for Citation Generation), a two-stage framework that introduces an explicit cognitive attribution map before answer generation. CAGE first trains a plug-and-play Cognitive Map Induction Model to construct answer-centered support subgraphs, aligning each semantic answer unit with supporting documents through explicit relations. A Structured Citation Reasoning Model then realizes these units as sentence-level claims with map-aligned citations. Experiments on ASQA, ELI5, and ExpertQA show that CAGE achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of attribution-space contraction and map-guided citation generation.
2607.24236.paper_summary_zh: 長篇問答越來越依賴檢索的證據來使大型語言模型的輸出可驗證，並且內嵌引用將主張追溯到來源文件。然而，現有系統經常附上主題相關但不足以支持其主張的引用。我們將歸因模糊性確定為一個結構性挑戰：端到端生成必須隱式解決組合主張--文件的分配，模糊證據邊界並增加證據邊界超限的風險，即主張超過引用支持。為了解決這一挑戰，我們提出了CAGE（認知歸因圖用於引用生成），這是一個兩階段框架，在答案生成之前引入明確的認知歸因圖。CAGE首先訓練一個即插即用的認知圖誘導模型，以構建以答案為中心的支持子圖，通過明確的關係將每個語義答案單元與支持文件對齊。然後，結構化引用推理模型將這些單元實現為具有地圖對齊引用的句子級主張。在ASQA、ELI5和ExpertQA上的實驗表明，CAGE達到了最先進的性能，展示了歸因空間收縮和地圖引導引用生成的有效性。
